summary: Rate-window oscillation during scheduled batched ingest causing intermittent 429s after auth refresh
description: Customer reports intermittent 429 responses during their nightly batched ingest run after they enabled short-lived credential rotation. Symptoms appear as small bursts of successful uploads followed by repeated 429s for 30-90s, then normal traffic resumes. The pattern repeats roughly every 5-8 minutes during the job window.
impact: Multiple failed batch chunks in nightly ETL job; downstream indexer saw partial data and required manual retries. Estimated 15% of batches failed during the 2-hour window. Customer requests guidance and a mitigation path to prevent data loss and reduce retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Set up a dedicated pool account with short-lived signed API keys (TTL ~ 5 minutes).
2) Run concurrent uploader workers that reauthenticate on TTL expiry and immediately restart chunk uploads without jitter.
3) Observe client-side logs showing simultaneous signed-key refresh and then a flood of requests to /v1/embeddings endpoint.
4) Check server responses: initial small window of OKs then a wave of 429s; repeating every few minutes as refill windows interact with auth refreshes.
logs: Gateway logs: token_accounting: window_refill=1610ms drift=+420ms; per-route-burst_used=1523; tenant_credit_left=480
Rate limiter trace (2026-03-10T02:14:23Z): owner=streamlytics-route-19 refill_epoch=1641 sawtooth_delta=+1.2s counts=[ok=312, throttled=47]
Auth service: issued short-lived key id=sk_tmp_4a2 exp=2026-03-10T02:19:00Z; multiple near-simultaneous refreshes from 10 workers
Customer uploader logs: 429 count spikes at 02:14:26Z, 02:21:35Z, 02:28:42Z (interval ~7m)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: simultaneous short-lived key rotation across uploader workers creates a burst that aligns with the rate-limiter refill epoch causing a sawtooth/oscillation effect.
Confirmed via trace correlation: gateway token window refills occur on a fixed epoch and the client's reauth fanout often fell within the same refill window after TTL expiry.

Observed additional contributing factor: dedicated-pool per-route burst pool was configured conservatively; tenant-level smoothing parameter (smoothing_factor) set to low value causing coarse refill granularity.
Reproduced in staging by simulating 12 workers reauthing at TTL expiry without jitter and running concurrent chunk uploads; saw identical repeating 429 pattern.

Temporary mitigation trial: staggered reauth in staging with +/- 60s jitter eliminated the oscillation. Increasing per-route burst pool size to 8x reduced visible throttles but did not fully remove sawtooth under worst-case fanout.

Found a gateway accounting edge-case: when a short-lived key is reused across HTTP/2 multiplexed connections the token-window bookkeeping occasionally double-counts the preflight for each stream; created issue INT-3392.
Logged related gateway PR that addressed double-counting: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/612 (fixes preflight-accounting on multiplexed streams).

resolution_notes: In-progress: applied tenant-side guidance to the customer (auth jitter + limited concurrent reauth). Scoped a controlled config change to the customer's dedicated pool to increase per-route burst allocation from 2->16 for nightly ingest windows; change scheduled 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC with rollback plan. Gateway double-counting bug fix merged and staged (PR #612). Customer reported immediate improvement after jitter; final verification pending post-maintenance run.
